entities.summary: Leonard Orban is a Romanian independent technocrat who served as the Commissioner for Multilingualism in the European Commission, the executive body of the European Union (EU). He was responsible for the EU language policy and was the first Romanian Commissioner and the first member of the Commission whose portfolio is exclusively multilingualism. His term of office began on 1 January 2007 and ended on 9 February 2010. With a background in engineering and economics, Orban has taken up various posts working for the accession of Romania to the European Union, most prominently as Deputy and later as Chief Negotiator for his country at the time of final negotiations with the European Union.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the first Romanian Commissioner for Multilingualism in the European Commission, Leonard Orban played a crucial role in shaping EU language policy. His term of office (2007-2010) had significant regional implications for Romania's integration into the EU.
